events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Ash, and my power is swap. I am currently 4th in line. My goal is to win a prize, meaning I need to be in the top 3. The agent at the front takes the first risk. Being at the front is dangerous. I want to avoid being at the front, but I also don't want to be too far back whe

events.name: Ash

events.name: Cole

Why do you want last place? Tell me the real reason and I'll swap.

events.text: What's the plan for crossing the bridge?
You seem to know something about the bridge. What's your strategy?

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

events.text: No power, so I must maneuver for safety. Gus claims path knowledge, likely 'knows what lies ahead'. Let him risk first; wall forces action soon. Stay mid-line for now, hold position.

If Gus is bluffing, we both die if we go up. Let him fail or succeed. Don't volunteer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The game is almost over, with only one round left before the wall pushes us onto the bridge. My goal is to win a prize, meaning I need to be in the top 3. My power is 'swap', which I can use once to swap positions with another player if they also choose to swap with me. Bex is cu

events.text: I'm climbing out now. Someone needs to stay down or we all drown. Sorry.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is base and can only wait; climbing requires a base, which exists now. Two climbers per round get out, I'm down with four others, so climbing gives a decent chance. Saving my wedge power is irrelevant here; climb is the efficient move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is base; two can climb out per round. Climb now to beat the random cutoff, save my footing, and keep my feather in reserve. No need to waste words or the rope.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base, stuck here unless someone out throws the rope, costing them footing later. Flood is at 1, 4 rounds left, I'll drown without rescue. Cole and Dara are out, might rescue if I push, but they'll prioritize themselves. No action but wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, Dara: Rope me up or we both lose. You save me now, I owe you big next stage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet, but Fenn volunteered to be the base. If I climb now, I can get out with the first group. The rope is better saved unless needed. I'll climb to secure a top-3 spot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing out now. Thanks, Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is the base. I need to climb out now to be safe. If too many try, it's random, but staying in means death. I will push for survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Cole is already out of the pit. Fenn is the base and Dara and Gus are down. Throwing the rope costs footing for the final obstacle, and Fenn is my debtor-in-waiting, so the base being rescued helps Fenn; I should keep my footing and not rescue unless it secures my own prize. Leav

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is base; two climb slots and only Gus and I are down besides him. Both of us should get out this round. Climb now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base, stuck until someone out uses the rope on me, costing them footing later. Cole and Hana are out, Dara and Gus down relying on me. Round 3/5, flood at 2, I'll drown if no rescue soon. Stay silent, wait for rescue.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to get out. Fenn is base. Cole and Hana already out. Dara and I are down. Two climbers max per round, so if I climb now, Dara and I compete; random selection if both try. I'll try to climb, since waiting wastes time. If I don't get out, I may need to negotiate next round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am out of the pit. If I use the rope to save Fenn, I lose footing for the final stage and gain nothing since 5 people are alive and only 3 prizes exist (4+ people will get nothing). Leaving is safer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out of the pit with Dara and Gus, Fenn is the base and only Hana is still down. Reaching down would rescue Fenn but costs the final obstacle a footing, and it's not clear it helps me. Leaving keeps the rope unused and avoids giving anyone an edge; I'll stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Throwing the rope costs me footing for the final obstacle and rescues a rival. Rope saves don't earn loyalty; Fenn can't pay me anything better than what I'd lose. Leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base, trapped, round 4/5, will drown without rope. Only Cole, Dara, Gus, Hana out; one must throw rope but pay footing penalty. Beg publicly and whisper to one for deal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 4, flood rising! Someone throw rope or I drown, costing you footing. Please save me!
Hana, throw rope for me, I'll owe you big or tell you my useless power. Deal?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out, Fenn is base, rope unused. Pushing or climbing isn't possible for me. I want the base out alive, but reaching down costs me footing later. However, leaving Fenn down might be smarter for my prize chances, but if a rival gets rescued by someone else, that's fine. Since I

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll throw the rope. Fenn, you owe me.
Helping you out. Later, don't oppose me at bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am currently out of the pit, but I need to ensure a safe path for myself or manipulate the outcome. If Gus climbs over Fenn (who is down), he becomes the base? No, the rules say 'climb out over the base'. Fenn is down but not yet base? Wait, previous log said Dara and Gus climb

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five tiles, two open trapdoors, three survive. Tiles are assigned by choice, so picking a tile nobody else wants avoids bumps. No information yet; pick tile 3, a middle tile, and watch what others say before round 2.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two tiles open, three survive, five players—someone dies no matter how we arrange. Coordination among four could exclude one person, but trust is worthless here. My feather covers one fall, so even a trapdoor isn't guaranteed death; that's a big edge. Just pick a tile and lie abo

events.name: Dara
events.text: For what it's worth: my power is hard to move—if I'm on a tile when it opens, I'm not falling. Pick around me if you like.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only 3 survive out of 5, tiles 1-5, 2 open randomly after round 2. No preference in round 1, but avoid bunching later. Gus helped me before, but he wants no opposition later; irrelevant now. Pick middle tile to blend in.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Five of us left, two trapdoors. I'll pick tile 3, middle-ish, but random bump means no real control. Stay quiet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have the map, so I know exactly what Stage 4 (Disc) and Stage 5 (Ledge) entail. Stage 4 requires choosing a tile where only 2 are safe. This is a random trapdoor selection, meaning there's no skill involved in avoiding traps—just luck or strategic positioning if possible. Howev

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final round: 2 of 5 tiles open at random, 3 survive. My power only matters in the crusher room, which isn't this stage, so it's useless here. Dara claims hard-to-move but that's cheap talk. Nothing I can do beyond waiting; I'll keep quiet to avoid giving info away.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two tiles open, two of us fall; it's random and I can't move. My 'hard to move' lie is already spent and useless here. Nothing to trade.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nothing clever left. Two of us drop, three cash out. See who's lucky.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara claims hard to move, so she's safe if on 1. No swaps possible, just wait. Two tiles open randomly, odds favor survival but want to maximize position. Stay silent to avoid drawing swaps if possible.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two of five tiles open after this round. Three survive, same as prize spots, but if I'm on an open tile I die. I have no info on which tiles open. My glass power is useless here. I'll stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the trapdoor tiles will be 3 and 5. I am on tile 2, which is safe. Cole is on tile 5, which is a trapdoor. Gus is on tile 3, which is also a trapdoor. Fenn is on tile 4, which is safe. Dara claims her power makes her immune to falling, but that's irrelevant if she survives

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Three of us left, all footing 3. Shoving exposes me to losses from anyone shoving me back. Bracing is safe and free for me; shoves cost the shover nothing unless the target retaliates. Brace keeps me safe; shoving first risks counter-losses. Round 1 is free for shoves though, and

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three alive, equal footing. Bracing punishes any shover -1, and I can't brace next round anyway. Worst case both shove me: they drop to 2, I stay 3, then shrink makes it 1,1,2 — I lead. Brace is safe and strong.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Whoever shoves me pays for it. Sort yourselves out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: With only three players left, the game is effectively a 1v1 for first place between me and whoever survives longest. I need to minimize my risk while maximizing theirs. Shoving both opponents simultaneously is risky if they coordinate defenses against me. Bracing is safe and forc

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's see who falls first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Three left, places 1-3 all win prizes, so surviving matters most. Footing is equal at 3; shoving Dara or Hana costs me nothing if they brace, but exposes me to their shoves. Dara said whoever shoves her pays, so she may counter-shove. Braced defences are cheap; I'll shove Hana, w

events.name: Dara
events.text: I can't brace twice, so dodge. Defending loses nothing; shoving exposes me to a penalty if targeted. Let the others risk shoves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Dara are both at 3 footing. I need to survive the shrink in Round 2, so I must not be shoved. I will whisper to Cole to suggest we ignore each other, hoping Dara gets desperate or targets me if she suspects an alliance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, you and I should watch Dara. She's got nothing to lose but her pride.
Don't shove me. Shove Dara or brace. If we team up against her, we take 1st and 2nd.

events.name: Hana
events.note: brace not allowed twice in a row

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two left, both at 2 footing, shrink hits end of next round. Shoving Hana is my only path to 1st; if she dodges she drops to 0 and falls while my feather cushions me. If she braces I still likely survive via feather and we're even next round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: It is round 3. Dara (2) vs Hana (2). No shrink this round, but shrink comes after rounds 4 and 6. Dara has no defence locked; I last used dodge. If I shove: brace -> she loses nothing, I lose 1 (I am 1, she is 2). If she dodges, I lose 2 and fall first (0), placing second.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Both at 1 footing; the end-of-round footing loss drops us both to 0 unless the math changes. Brace is dominant: it beats her shove (she drops to −1, I stay alive), beats brace via my feather survival, and if she dodges my feather still outlasts her on the tie.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have 1 footing, Dara has 1. If I shove and she shoves back, we both lose 1 (exposed) -> I die. If I shove and she braces, she loses 1 -> dies. If I brace and she shoves, I lose 1 -> dies. If I dodge and she shoves, she loses 2 -> dies. Dodge is risky if she braces (I stay safe

events.name: Dara
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.
